actions: Run `pixi run -e pyforge-scribe scribe-install-nightly-trigger` on the machine that holds all three surfaces the nightly compile needs (this checkout's `.claude/memory/`, your own per-user session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-repo>/*.jsonl`, and the gitignored `.claude/data/pyforge-scribe/` graph store) — this installs and enables the checked-in systemd-user timer.

If the installer warns that linger is not enabled (`loginctl show-user $USER --property=Linger` reads `Linger=no`), run `loginctl enable-linger $USER` so the timer keeps firing at 02:30 even when you are fully logged out overnight, not only right after your next login.

If your `GraphStore` driver is PostgreSQL (`PYFORGE_GRAPHSTORE_OWNER=steward`), export that variable in the shell you run the installer from BEFORE installing, so it gets baked into the rendered systemd unit — and re-run the installer any time you change that setting, since the baked-in value does not update itself.

Let the timer fire on its own schedule for at least 4 consecutive nights, then confirm it: check `~/.cache/scribe-nightly-compile.log` (or `journalctl --user -u pyforge-scribe-nightly-compile.service`) for 4 distinct 02:30 runs, or run `pixi run -e local-recipes scribe-graph-freshness-check` and confirm it reports the graph store as fresh across that period. This is spec-pyforge-scribe's own CAP-2 success signal and cannot be verified from the repo alone — it requires your machine and real elapsed time.
